title: prez strip_comments truncates at a '/*' inside a string, so refuse_external never sees the rest of the theme
body:
`prez`'s `strip_comments` truncates the source at any `/*` it cannot close, so everything after it is never scanned by `refuse_external`. A `/*` inside a string literal triggers this, and the browser does not agree that it is a comment. **Shipped in 2.8.0. Distinct from issue 0014.**

## The defect

`theme.rs:498-517`:

```rust
match rest[at..].find("*/") {
  Some(end) => { /* keep newlines, continue */ }
  None => return out,
}
```

`strip_comments` is a naive scanner: it has no notion of string literals, so `content: "/*"` reads as an unterminated comment. It then returns everything BEFORE that point and discards the remainder. `refuse_external` scans the truncated string, so **any external reference after the offending token is never examined at all.**

This is a different failure from 0014 and needs a different fix. 0014 is *the scanner sees the text and the needle set does not match it*. This is *the scanner never sees the text*.

## Measured, on `opt/prez/crate/target/release/prez`, with both controls

| Theme CSS | rc | Result |
| --------- | -- | ------ |
| `body{color:red}` + `@import "https://cdn/x.css";` | 2 | refused. **Red control** -- the check is wired and running |
| `body{color:red}` | 0 | built. **Green control** -- rc=0 means built, not silently errored |
| `/* oops` (unterminated) then the `@import` | 0 | **BUILDS** |
| `body{content:"/*"}` then the `@import` | 0 | **BUILDS** |

`grep -o '@import[^;]*;'` over the artifact from the last case returns `@import "https://cdn/x.css";`.

## Why the last row is the serious one

The unterminated-comment case is mostly self-neutralising: a browser also treats the rest of the file as commented out, so nothing is fetched. **The string-literal case is not.** A browser parses `content: "/*"` correctly as a string, so the `@import` after it is live CSS and **the artifact fetches from the network when opened** -- which is exactly what `theme.rs`'s own module note calls "the load-bearing rule of the whole feature, not a nicety", and what `help/prez.md` sells as an artifact that "opens offline ... in five years".

`content: "/*"` is not an exotic construct. It is the kind of thing that appears in a reset or a decorative rule.

## Found how

While verifying `cc`'s WP-01 report for ST0017. `cc` had written a characterisation test in the new `artifact` crate, `an_unterminated_comment_does_not_swallow_a_reference_silently`, flagging the truncation as a policy nobody had chosen on purpose. Probing that flag against the shipped binary found the string-literal path, which is the half that survives contact with a browser.

## Relationship to ST0017

`artifact`'s `strip_comments` is currently **byte-identical** to prez's, deliberately -- WP-01 is a pure move and copies the behaviour hole included. So this defect is about to exist in two tools rather than one, exactly as recorded for 0014 in `design.md` 1.3.

The fix belongs with R2's needle-set decision in WP-03, where the scanner is being specified anyway. **Filed separately from 0014 so that R2's landing cannot be read as closing it** -- fixing the needle set does nothing for a scanner that never receives the text.


---

## CLOSED 2026-09-09 -- ST0017/WP-03, AC-3.5

Fixed in `crates/artifact/src/theme.rs`. `strip_comments` now tracks string literals, so `content: "/*"` is a string and not a comment that never closes; the `@import` after it is scanned and refused. A string ends at its quote **or at a newline**, so one stray quote cannot switch off comment stripping for the rest of the file -- which would have re-opened this exact hole one character wide, and has its own test.

**And the serious half's sibling changed behaviour on purpose: a genuinely unterminated comment is now REFUSED by name, not truncated.** Truncation is defensible on browser semantics and indefensible as silence -- `IN-AG-NO-SILENT-001`, on the scan that holds the offline guarantee. The refusal names the comment rather than the reference, because the theme is malformed and that is the smaller, truer claim.

**The test that recorded this hole asked to be inverted rather than deleted, and was.** `an_unterminated_comment_truncates_the_scan_which_is_a_known_hole` is now `an_unterminated_comment_is_refused_rather_than_ending_the_scan_in_silence`, keeping its fixture. Red-proved against the old implementation with the injection's application proved first; E7 and E8 were among the eight it decided wrongly. Artifact level: both fixtures went rc=0 to rc=2.
